sentences.text:
* * * *
Pankaj Jain, J.

[1] These are cross appeals arising out of a claim petition filed under Section 166 of the Motor
Vehicles Act, 1988, whereby claimants sought compensation on account of death of Gaurav Jain son
of Nirmal Kumar Jain in a motor vehicular accident dated 06.12.2014 at a young age of 28 years.
 1 of 4
Fao-1793-2016
 2016 and
Fao-5950-2016

[2] The Tribunal ribunal partly allowed the petition and awarded a compensation of 89,69,960/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum for the period commencing from the date of filing of the claim petition till the date of actual realization.

[3] FAO-1793-2016  2016 is at the be  behest  hest of the Insurance Company,
challenging the findings recorded by the Tribunal on Issue No.1 i.e. negligence of the driver of the insured vehicle and on Issue No.2 i.e. quantum of the compensation.
[4] FAO-5950-2016 is at the behest of the claimants, w who ho are seeking enhancement of the compensation.

[5] Learned counsel for the Insurance Company submits that Tribunal erred in returning finding on Issue No.1 against the driver of the insured vehicle merely on relying upon the registration of the FIR.
He submits that the mechanical report on record has been totally ignored.

sentences.text: 2 [6] I have heard learned counsel for the parties and have carefully gone through record(s) of the case.
[7] Learned counsel for the Insurance Company does not dispute that FIR (Exhibit (Exhibi P-8) was registered qua accident in which Gaurav Jain lost his life.
PW3-ASI PW3 ASI Karambir Singh, Investigating Officer, was examined by the claimants.
He proved FIR as well as deposed that report under Section 173 Cr.P.C. has been filed by him.
He also pr proved oved impounding of vehicle insured with the appellant from the spot of occurrence.

PW4 PW4-Rohit Rohit Kapoor, eye witness of the accident, appeared and deposed regarding rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle being cause of 2 of 4 FAO-1793-2016 2016 and FAO-5950-2016 accident.
He also testified that the driver was apprehended on the spot by public but he managed to flee.
The best person to rebut the aforesaid evidence on record was respondent No.1 i.e. driver of the offending vehicle.
Admittedly, he opted not to appear.
[8] In view thereof, this Court finds that no fault can be found with the findings recorded by the Tribunal on Issue No.1.
The same are accordingly affirmed.
[9] Both the parties are aggrieved of findings recorded by the Tribunal on Issue No.2.
No.2 A lot has been argued by the counsel representting rival parties regarding the salary of the deceased.
In the considered opinion of this Court, salary of deceased Gaurav Jain was proved by his salary slip for the month of October, 2014 and November 2014 (Exhibits P P-16 & P-17).

17). 
As per Exhibit Exhibi P-17, 17, his last pay drawn was 42,000/-.
In the considered opinion of this Court, Tribunal rightly assessed the monthly salary of the deceased--Gaurav Jain as 42,000/- and applied deduction of 1/3rd.
Future prospects of 40% need to be awarded instead oof 50%.

In terms of ratio of law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of 'Sarla Sarla Verma and others versus Delhi Transport Corporation and another another', 2009(3) RCR 77 multiplier of '17' needs to bee applied instead of '18'..

sentences.text: Nothing (Civil) 77, Nothi has been awarded on account of loss of estate.
18,000/- is awarded for loss of estate..
The amount of 25,000/- awarded on account of funeral expenses is maintained.
The amount of 1,00,000/ 1,00,000/- to each of the claimants for loss of love and affection needs to be substituted and modified by awarding 48,000/-- to each of the claimants.
3 of 4 FAO-1793-2016 2016 and FAO-5950-2016 [10] With the aforesaid modifications, the appeals are disposed off.
The interest shall abide by the award passed by the Tribunal.
Out ooff the total compensation awarded hereinabove, 50,00,000/- shall be paid to claimant-Kanika Kanika Jain and rest of the amount shall be distributed equally amongst the parents.
[11] All pending miscellaneous application(s), if any, also stand disposed off.
[12] Photocopy of this order be placed on the file of connected case.
(PANKAJ JAIN) JUDGE 22.12.2025 'R. Sharma' Whether speaking/ reasoned : Yes/No
